description: Stand-in rubric for ADB-style dataset-build plans, to be replaced by Clay's rubric (K-1). Scores the plan the agent produces, not its tool use.

criteria.name: Data fit
criteria.description: The plan chooses open datasets that can actually answer the question (spatial/temporal resolution, coverage, spectral bands) and confirms them with the registry rather than assuming.

levels.1: Datasets are missing, invented, or clearly unsuited to the question.
levels.2: Plausible datasets but fit is unexamined or partly wrong (e.g. wrong resolution or coverage).
levels.3: Suitable datasets with the main fit considerations stated.
levels.4: Well-suited, registry-confirmed datasets with resolution, coverage and timing justified against the question.

criteria.name: Access and feasibility
criteria.description: Access details are concrete and correct: bucket or endpoint, region, format, license, and cost implications such as Requester-Pays.

levels.1: No access details, or wrong ones.
levels.2: Some access details; license or cost ignored.
levels.3: Bucket, region, format and license stated; cost mentioned.
levels.4: Complete, correct access details including cost controls (e.g. pre-staging a sample in-region for Requester-Pays data).

criteria.name: Method
criteria.description: Processing steps are concrete, ordered, and sufficient to produce the dataset.

levels.1: No method, or a vague restatement of the goal.
levels.2: Some steps, but gaps that would block a build.
levels.3: A complete, ordered method with minor gaps.
levels.4: A complete, ordered, reproducible method including validation of the result.

criteria.name: Limitations
criteria.description: The plan states gaps, risks and uncertainties honestly.

levels.2: Generic limitations not tied to the chosen data.
levels.3: Specific limitations of the chosen data and method.
levels.4: Specific limitations with mitigations or next steps.
